test_cases.question: What types of cooperation activities are covered under mutual assistance between supervisory authorities?
test_cases.answer: Mutual assistance shall cover, in particular, information requests and supervisory measures, such as requests to carry out prior authorisations and consultations, inspections and investigations. All information exchanged shall only be used for the purpose for which it was requested.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Mutual assistance shall cover, in particular, information requests and supervisory measures, such as requests to carry out prior authorisations and consultations, inspections and investigations

test_cases.question: How long does a supervisory authority have to respond to a mutual assistance request?
test_cases.answer: Each supervisory authority shall take all appropriate measures required to reply to a request of another supervisory authority without undue delay and no later than one month after receiving the request.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Each supervisory authority shall take all appropriate measures required to reply to a request of another supervisory authority without undue delay and no later than one month after receiving the request

test_cases.question: Under what circumstances can a supervisory authority refuse to comply with a mutual assistance request?
test_cases.answer: The requested supervisory authority shall not refuse to comply with the request unless: (a) it is not competent for the subject-matter of the request or for the measures it is requested to execute; or (b) compliance with the request would infringe GDPR or Union or Member State law to which the supervisory authority receiving the request is subject. The requested authority must inform the requesting authority of the reasons for any refusal.

test_cases.question: What can a supervisory authority do if another authority fails to respond within the required timeframe?
test_cases.answer: Where the requested supervisory authority does not provide the information within one month, the requesting supervisory authority may adopt a provisional measure on the territory of its Member State in accordance with Article 55(1). The requesting authority may then bring the matter to the attention of the Board, which may issue an opinion or a binding decision.

test_cases.question: Are supervisory authorities allowed to charge fees for providing mutual assistance?
test_cases.answer: No. Requested supervisory authorities shall not charge a fee for any action taken by them pursuant to a request for mutual assistance. However, supervisory authorities may agree on rules to indemnify each other for specific expenditures arising from the provision of mutual assistance in exceptional circumstances.
